goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`; .map always returns an array so `|| []` is dead and unresolved ids become undefined entries (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural-id hydration branch in `store.js.es6`, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always return an Array when `obj[k]` is an array, so `hydrated || []` is indeed effectively dead code in the normal case. More importantly, unlike the singular `_id` branch (which only replaces the field when `hydrated` is truthy), the `_ids` branch *always* deletes the original `..._ids` field and assigns the mapped result. If `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id, the mapped array will contain `undefined` entries, and the original ids are lost, which is a correctness regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update ignores the request body and just re-serializes, so the client saveChanges/embedding.update({}) persists nothing (P3, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddingController#update (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:11-13), the action does not read or apply any params; it simply re-renders the current @embedding OpenStruct via EmbeddingSerializer. There is no persistence logic (and @embedding itself is not an ActiveRecord model). On the client side, admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 defines a saveChanges action that calls this.get('embedding').update({}), which would issue a PUT but, given the server implementation, cannot persist anything. This is directly verifiable from the diff (PUT route added, controller update is a no-op).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb — no validates_uniqueness_of :host and no unique index; duplicate hosts let record_for_host pick an arbitrary category nondeterministically (P2, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, EmbeddableHost has only a format validation on :host and the migration creates embeddable_hosts(host, category_id) with no unique index on host. The lookup used for authorization/routing (EmbeddableHost.record_for_host) does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no ORDER, so if duplicate host rows exist (possibly with different category_id), `.first` can return an arbitrary row depending on DB/query plan. This makes the chosen category (and allowed-host decision if a duplicate were deleted/added) nondeterministic. Nothing in the diff prevents duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:21 — `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` with no strong-params require/permit raises NoMethodError when the wrapper key is missing (P2, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code directly dereferences nested params: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If the `:embeddable_host` wrapper key is absent or nil (e.g., malformed request), this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil[:host]`). The diff shows no guard (`params.require(:embeddable_host)`) or fallback handling, so the reported failure mode is real and directly attributable to the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 and embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — only class-ancestry assertions; create/update/destroy, category defaulting, invalid host, host_allowed? unverified; no spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb (P1, conf 95)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add controller specs that only assert class ancestry (admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb), so that part is factually accurate but it’s a test-coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the code. Additionally, the finding claims there is “no spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb”, but the diff clearly *adds* spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb with host trimming and host_allowed? behavior tests. Because the key claim about missing model spec is incorrect and the rest is not a concrete defect, this is not a REAL problem in the diff under the stated criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:41 — `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` ignores the server-coerced category_id, so a blank selection shows an empty badge until reload (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host`’s `save()` action, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`, but the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly coerces a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. After a successful save, the component sets the relationship with `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` using the *pre-save UI value*, not the server-returned/coerced value. If `categoryId` is blank/null (which is allowed because `cantSave` only checks `host` and not `categoryId`), `findById(null)` will yield nothing, so `host.category` becomes unset and the template `{{category-badge host.category}}` can show empty until a reload/reload of relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/client.en.yml — `admin.embedding.edit` key added but never referenced; no empty-state/description copy for the new admin page (P3, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin.embedding.edit` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, but the new templates/components reference `admin.embedding.title`, `host`, `category`, `add_host`, and `confirm_delete` (via `I18n.t`). There is no reference to `admin.embedding.edit` anywhere in the added JS/HBS in this diff, so the key appears unused. However, an unused i18n key and lack of empty-state/description copy are not clear correctness bugs or defects introduced by the code (they’re more of a cleanup/product suggestion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb + spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the two files' contents are fully swapped; unrelated churn that misleads readers and path-based lookup (P2, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category-related fabricators, i.e. the contents are effectively swapped relative to filenames. However, this is not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone: Fabrication typically loads all fabricator files (and associations like `category` are resolved when fabricating, not necessarily at definition time), and there’s no evidence in the diff of any path-based `require` relying on these specific filenames. So the finding is largely about confusing/unconventional organization rather than a proven correctness bug introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-206 — unrequested app-wide `_ids` hydration change: every key ending in _ids is now deleted and replaced unconditionally, unlike the guarded singular branch (P1, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In `_hydrateEmbedded` the new plural match `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` adds an `_ids` branch that always does `delete obj[k]` after mapping ids through `_lookupSubType`. Unlike the singular `_id` branch (which only deletes the key when a hydrated object is found), the plural branch deletes the original id list unconditionally, even if `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for some/all ids (e.g., when the related records aren’t present in `root`). This can silently drop the raw `*_ids` data and replace it with an array of missing objects, introducing a correctness regression in the generic store hydration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — `type.replace('_','-')` in the shared adapter is unnecessary (model registered as 'embeddable-host') and replaces only the first underscore (P2, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ADMIN_MODELS` contains dash-form names (e.g. `site-customization`, `embeddable-host`). Changing the check to `type.replace('_','-')` is plausibly needed to handle cases where `type` arrives underscored (e.g. `embeddable_host`), and nothing in the diff proves `type` is always already registered/passed as `embeddable-host`. While it’s true that `String#replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore, the diff shows only admin model names with at most one underscore-equivalent segment, so there’s no verifiable breakage. The “unnecessary” part is not demonstrably true from the diff and the “first underscore only” point is at most a hypothetical edge case, not a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard dropped with no EmbeddableHost equivalent, silently widening expandable_first_post? (P2, conf 70)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check in `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but `embeddable_hosts` site setting is also removed entirely and host-allowance is moved to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — `category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes an Integer where PostCreator's :category option expects a name/slug, so embedded topics land uncategorized and the headline host-to-category feature is a no-op (P0, conf 85)

In Discourse, the `PostCreator` API commonly receives `category` as a category *id* (the param name is `category`, but the value is typically the integer id), and the rest of this diff (controllers/serializers/UI) consistently uses `category_id` integers. Nothing in the diff indicates `PostCreator` expects a name/slug instead, so the finding’s core claim isn’t verifiable from the provided changes and is likely a misreading of the API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` never downcases the bound param and stored hosts are never normalized, so mixed-case hosts silently fail the allow check; also an unindexed scan per embed request (P1, conf 85)
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the query uses `lower(host) = ?` but the bound parameter `host` is not lowercased/normalized, so mixed-case referer hosts may not match despite intended case-insensitive comparison. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12-19 — record_for_host returns false on failure but nil/record otherwise: three shapes for one contract, so .nil?-style callers are wrong (P2, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` can return `false` (on parse/host absence) or an ActiveRecord object or `nil` (no match). However, all usages added/modified in this diff treat the result in a way that is correct for both `false` and `nil`: `host_allowed?` uses `.present?`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)`. No `.nil?`-style callers are shown in the diff, and in Ruby both `false` and `nil` are falsey so this inconsistency is not a verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6-7 — before_validation strips scheme/path but keeps the port while lookup compares to uri.host (no port), so a host saved with a port can never match though the regex allows ports (P2, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbeddableHost.before_validation the code strips scheme and path but not the port (e.g. "http://example.com:3000/x" becomes "example.com:3000"). However EmbeddableHost.record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI() and then uses uri.host, which excludes the port ("example.com"). The DB lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored host containing a port can never match an incoming URL for that host, even though the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port. This is a concrete mismatch introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — `t.integer :category_id, null: false` with no FK, no index, and no UNIQUE on host: duplicate hosts and dangling category ids are both representable (P1, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.integer :category_id, null: false` and `t.string :host, null: false` but defines no foreign key to `categories`, no indexes, and no uniqueness constraint on `host`. In the same diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record’s `category_id`; if duplicate host rows exist, the chosen category becomes arbitrary. Also, without an FK, rows can reference deleted/nonexistent categories, which can surface as `host.category` being nil in the admin UI (`{{category-badge host.category}}`). These integrity issues are directly representable with the schema as added in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196,200 — `obj[k].map` assumes an array (throws on scalar/null) and pluralize is naive +"s", so category_ids hydrates into `categorys` no template reads (P1, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: The new code path in `store.js` only calls `obj[k].map(...)` when the key matches `/_ids$/`, which (by convention and by the new `EmbeddingSerializer` using `embed: :ids`) should always be an array of ids. The diff does not show any payload producing a scalar/null for an `_ids` field, so the “throws on scalar/null” claim is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here. Additionally, the finding’s claim that pluralization is naive `+"s"` (leading to `categorys`) is not supported by the diff: it calls `self.pluralize(subType)`, and no implementation is shown/changed here to justify that assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 — `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` puts the NOT NULL default in the controller, so every other creation path hits a raw DB constraint error (P2, conf 70)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does put the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, while the migration defines `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` and the `EmbeddableHost` model does not validate/preset `category_id`. However, within this diff, all shown creation paths either set `category_id` (migration inserts with `category_id`, fabricator includes `category`, UI saves go through this controller which applies the fallback) or don’t create records. The finding’s claim that “every other creation path” will hit a DB constraint error is speculative and not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:17-20 — `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` unbounded materialization with no index and no pagination path on admin page load (P3, conf 70)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding the code sets `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, which will indeed load all embeddable hosts and sort them. However, this is the intended behavior for an admin “allowed hosts” management screen (it needs the full list to render), and the diff doesn’t establish that the table can grow large enough for this to be a clear defect. The claim about “no index” is verifiable (the migration adds no index on `host`), but lack of an index/pagination here is a speculative performance concern rather than a concrete, verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:60 — removing the explicit embeddable_hosts.blank? guard makes fail-closed behavior incidental to host_allowed?'s falsy return, with no test for the empty-table case (P2, conf 60)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the old explicit `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` guard was removed, but the new check `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` already fail-closes when the table is empty: `host_allowed?` is `record_for_host(...).present?`, and with no matching records it returns `false`, triggering the same `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess` path. So the diff does not introduce a correctness/security bug for the empty-table case; it just changes the specific error reason/message. While it’s true there isn’t a targeted spec asserting “referer present + empty embeddable_hosts table”, that is a test coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11 — the PUT handler mutates nothing while the client presents a saveChanges path, so the "edit" half of the feature is presented as working but is dead (P2, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb the `update` action (PUT /admin/customize/embedding) simply re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct via `render_serialized` and does not read params or persist any changes. On the client side, app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that PUT endpoint and receive a successful response even though nothing is actually updated. This is a verifiable no-op “save” path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — expandable_first_post? now returns true on sites with zero embeddable hosts; no EmbeddableHost.exists? substitute for the removed guard (P3, conf 65)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. This does not make the method return `true` merely because there are zero embeddable hosts; it still requires `has_topic_embed?` to be true (i.e., the topic is an embedded topic). The removed `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` guard corresponds to the removal of that site setting and the move to the `EmbeddableHost` model; there’s no verifiable defect in the diff showing that `expandable_first_post?` must be gated by `EmbeddableHost.exists?` rather than by `has_topic_embed?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24 — `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts site-setting into SQL; a quote in the value breaks the migration or injects arbitrary SQL as the migration role (P1, conf 95)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, and then constructs SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is inserted directly inside single quotes with no escaping/quoting helper, any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will either break the migration or could be interpreted as additional SQL. This is a verifiable SQL-injection / unsafe-SQL-construction pattern in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 — case-mismatched lookup silently denies correctly-configured hosts (fail-closed availability bug, not a bypass) (P2, conf 95)
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9,14,19 — missing nil/param guards yield staff-triggerable 500s (NoMethodError) rather than 404/422 (P3, conf 95)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `update` and `destroy` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without checking for `nil`. If an invalid/nonexistent `:id` is provided, this will raise `NoMethodError` (e.g., `undefined method 'host=' for nil:NilClass` or `undefined method 'destroy' for nil:NilClass`) producing a 500 instead of a 404.

Additionally, `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` exists and does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]`; if `embeddable_host` is missing, it will also raise `NoMethodError`, again yielding a 500 rather than a 422. These are directly verifiable from the diff and are staff-triggerable via malformed requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-43 — the category argument type changed from name-string to integer id with zero tests; nothing asserts the created topic's category (P1, conf 80)

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:66-70 — `Fabricate(:embeddable_host, host: 'https://example.com/1234')` is normalized to example.com by before_validation, so the "host with a path" test no longer tests path handling (P2, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` callback strips protocol and any path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). The spec setup in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` fabricates `EmbeddableHost` records including `host: 'https://example.com/1234'`, but when the record is saved by `Fabricate`, that value will be normalized and persisted as `example.com`. Therefore the “multiple hosts” scenario no longer exercises the behavior of matching an allowed-host entry that includes a path; it only tests matching against the normalized host. This is a verifiable loss of test coverage relative to what the fixture suggests it is testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 — all fabricators/specs use lowercase hosts, so the un-downcased bound param stays green in tests while failing in production (P1, conf 85)
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the new plural-hydration branch has no JS test in this diff (P2, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new behavior in `store.js.es6` to hydrate `*_ids` into pluralized embedded objects, and there is no corresponding JavaScript unit test added for that branch. However, “no test added” is not a verifiable correctness/bug/security defect in the code itself; it’s a process/coverage concern and cannot be confirmed as a real problem solely from the diff (the project may rely on existing tests or different test layers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — no test covers basePath underscore normalization; single-underscore replace silently misroutes multi-word admin models (P3, conf 80)

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, silently destroying existing rows on any re-run or partially-applied deploy (P0, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the table is created with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the adapter to drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That means if the migration is ever re-executed while the table exists (e.g., due to a failed/partial migration run where the schema_migrations row wasn’t recorded, or a manual re-run), any existing `embeddable_hosts` rows would be deleted without warning. The diff shows no need for `force: true` here since this is a new table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29 — `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts','embed_category')` inside `def change` is irreversible and raises IrreversibleMigration on rollback, leaving settings unrecoverable (P0, conf 95)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` defines `def change` but contains multiple raw `execute` statements, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot auto-reverse `execute` calls, so attempting to rollback this migration will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` (and even conceptually, deleting those rows loses data needed to restore prior settings). This is a verifiable irreversibility introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29 — expand+contract violation: settings deleted in the same migration that creates the table, so un-restarted app servers reading SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts 403 all embeds during the rolling deploy window (P1, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` both (1) migrates data out of the `site_settings` rows `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` into the new `embeddable_hosts` table and then (2) deletes those `site_settings` rows in the same migration (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). In the pre-diff code (shown removed/changed elsewhere in this diff), embed authorization depended on `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` and would raise when it is blank. During a rolling deploy window where DB migrations run before all app servers are on the new code, any still-running old code would see the deleted setting as blank and start rejecting embeds (403). That’s an expand/contract safety issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22 — no strip on split values, so CRLF-entered settings store a trailing carriage return in host and never match (P2, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the old setting value is split with `val.split("\n")` and each `h` is inserted directly into `embeddable_hosts` via raw SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`). If the original `site_settings.value` used CRLF line endings, each line (except possibly the last) will include a trailing `\r`, e.g. `"eviltrout.com\r"`. Because the migration bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model callbacks/validations (which also don’t strip whitespace/\r anyway), those rows would be stored with the `\r` and later `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against a clean `uri.host`, causing host matching to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:16 — `cmd_tuples` is a PG::Result-only API, adapter-locking the migration, and the guard is applied here but not to the two unguarded [0] accesses above (P2, conf 75)

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — migrated rows all get one guessed category_id (possibly 0 or a deleted category) under NOT NULL with no FK, producing orphans belongs_to resolves to nil (P1, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: The migration intentionally assigns a single category_id to all migrated hosts based on the prior global `embed_category` setting, which matches the old configuration model. It also explicitly falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` if the computed `category_id` is 0, so the claim that rows may get category_id 0 is not supported by the code path shown. Lack of a foreign key means categories can be deleted later and leave dangling IDs, but that’s a general schema choice and not a concrete defect introduced by this diff, nor is it verifiable from this migration alone.
